facts.statement: The genus and type species Abelisaurus comahuensis were named and described by José Bonaparte and Fernando Emilio Novas in 1985.
facts.quote: Coining the type species Abelisaurus comahuensis, both genus and species were named and described by Argentine paleontologists José Bonaparte and Fernando Emilio Novas in 1985.

facts.statement: The generic name honors Roberto Abel, who discovered the type specimen and was the former director of the provincial Museum of Cipolletti in Argentina.
facts.quote: The generic name recognizes Roberto Abel as the discoverer of the type specimen, and also as the former director of the provincial Museum of Cipolletti in Argentina, where the specimen is housed.

facts.statement: The holotype fossil MC 11098 was uncovered in 1983 at the Lago Pellegrini quarries in Argentina.
facts.quote: The holotype, MC 11098, was in 1983 uncovered at the "Cantera de la Pala Mécanica"-site in the Lago Pellegrini quarries exploited by Abel since 1975.

facts.statement: Abelisaurus lived during the early Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous Period, approximately 83 to 80 million years ago.
facts.quote: The Anacleto is a geologic formation in South America, dating from the early Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous Period, between 83 and 80 million years ago.

facts.statement: Locally, Abelisaurus fossils have been found in the Campanian Allen Formation, which creates uncertainty about its precise stratigraphic position.
facts.quote: However, locally Abelisaurus is known to have come from the Sr. Fernandez field, which is in the Campanian Allen Formation, which makes its stratigraphic position unclear.

facts.statement: The known skull of Abelisaurus could be estimated to be over 85 cm long.
facts.quote: Despite the missing pieces, it could be estimated at over 85 cm long.

facts.statement: The premaxilla of Abelisaurus bore four small teeth, while the maxilla behind it held at least seven, possibly up to thirteen, larger teeth.
facts.quote: The front snout bone, the premaxilla, bore four relatively small teeth. The maxilla behind it had at least seven, but perhaps as many as thirteen, larger teeth.

facts.statement: Abelisaurus was a carnivorous dinosaur with two small rough crests on its head, but these were not as well-defined as those found in other members of its family.
facts.quote: Abelisaurus fue un dinosaurio carnívoro con dos pequeñas crestas rugosas sobre su cabeza, pero no del tipo bien definido como la que tienen otros miembros de su familia.

facts.statement: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul proposed that Abelisaurus hunted titanosaurian sauropods like Antarctosaurus and Neuquensaurus.
facts.quote: In 2010, Paul proposed that Abelisaurus hunted titanosaurian sauropods, such as Antarctosaurus, Pellegrinisaurus, Barrosasaurus and Neuquensaurus.

facts.statement: Bonaparte and Novas placed Abelisaurus in the family Abelisauridae in 1985, initially considering it a member of the Carnosauria.
facts.quote: Bonaparte and Novas placed Abelisaurus in the newly created family Abelisauridae in 1985. They thought it was a member of the Carnosauria.

facts.statement: Subsequent research showed that abelisaurids, including Abelisaurus, belong to the Neoceratosauria rather than the modern sense of Carnosauria.
facts.quote: They showed that abelisaurids were not carnosaurs in the modern sense, but belonged to the Neoceratosauria instead.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Abelisaurus might actually be a carcharodontosaurid, though this hypothesis is considered unlikely by most researchers.
facts.quote: However, this is thought unlikely.

facts.statement: Abelisaurus was a bipedal carnivore estimated to reach about 7.4 meters in length, though this size is uncertain due to the incompleteness of the fossil record.
facts.quote: It was a bipedal carnivore that probably reached about 7.4 m in length, although this is uncertain as it is known from only one partial skull.

facts.statement: Abelisaurus had a proportionally longer preorbital opening than tyrannosaurs or other Jurassic and Cretaceous dinosaurs.
facts.quote: El orificio anterorbital es proporcionalmente más largo que en los tiranosáuridos e incluso que otros dinosaurios jurásicos o cretácicos.

facts.statement: The squamosal bone projecting backward with a ventrally directed quadrate jugal process places Abelisaurus with ceratosaurians rather than tyrannosaurs.
facts.quote: El escamoso que proyecta casi hasta atrás con un proceso cuadrado yugal dirigido ventralmente, lo colocan con los ceratosáuridos y no en los tiranosáuridos.

facts.statement: Abelisaurus had a prominent interorbital region where the lacrimal and postorbital bones contacted to form a projection on the orbit.
facts.quote: La región interorbital más prominente llegando a contactar con los hueso lacrimal y postorbital construyendo un tipo de proyección en la órbita.

facts.statement: The high orbital foramen combined with the previously noted formation resulted in a circumference that was barely open ventrally.
facts.quote: El foramen orbital es muy alto que con la formación anteriormente señalada dan una circunferencia apenas abierta ventralmente.

facts.statement: The horizontal ramus of the maxilla was thick to accommodate laterally flattened teeth.
facts.quote: La rama horizontal del maxilar gruesa para la inserción de los dientes aplanados lateralmente.

facts.statement: Abelisaurus had a narrow interorbital space caused by contact between the lacrimal and postorbital bones, distinct from Tyrannosaurus and Daspletosaurus.
facts.quote: El espacio interorbital estrecho, resultado del contacto entre los huesos lagrimal y postorbital, distinto al de Tyrannosaurus y Daspletosaurus.

facts.statement: The low temporal fenestra was much more open than in tyrannosaurs.
facts.quote: La ventana temporal baja muy abierta más que en los tiranosáuridos.

facts.statement: The preorbital region of Abelisaurus was notably different from tyrannosaurs, featuring a large difference in magnitude with a long opening and a reduced space between this opening and the external nose.
facts.quote: La región anterorbital es notablemente diferente al de los tiranosáuridos, con una gran diferencia entre las magnitudes, con una abertura larga y un espacio entre esta y la nariz externa reducido.

facts.statement: Roberto Abel discovered the remains of Abelisaurus in 1983.
facts.quote: Roberto Abel, antiguo director del Museo Provincial Carlos Ameghino de Río Negro, donde los restos del animal estuvieron almacenados hasta su estudio, lo halló en 1983

facts.statement: José Fernando Bonaparte and Fernando Novas named the genus Abelisaurus in 1985 after its discoverer and named the species comahuensis after the Comahue region of Patagonia, Argentina, where it was found.
facts.quote: Al estudiarlo en 1985 José Fernando Bonaparte y Fernando Novas le colocaron el nombre genérico Abelisaurus en honor a su descubridor y llamaron a la especie comahuensis debido a Comahue, región de la Patagonia Argentina, donde fue hallado.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen MC 11078 was unearthed in 1983 at the "Cantera de la Pala Mecánica" site near Lago Pellegrini, which Abel had explored since 1975.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotipo, MC 11078, fue desenterrado en 1983 en la "Cantera de la Pala Mecánica", sitio a orillas del Lago Pellegrini explorado por Abel desde 1975.

facts.statement: The only fossil remains are of a partial skull lacking the mandible, which is incomplete especially on the right side.
facts.quote: El único resto fósil es un cráneo parcial al que le falta la mandíbula, incompleto, especialmente en el lado derecho.

facts.statement: Despite missing pieces, the skull can be estimated to measure about 86 cm in length.
facts.quote: A pesar de las piezas faltantes se puede estimar que MEDIRÍA unos 86 cm de largo.

facts.statement: Although no crests or horns are present on the skull like in other found abelisaurids such as Carnotaurus, it is presumed they existed, likely made of keratin and thus not fossilized.
facts.quote: Aunque no hay crestas o cuernos en el cráneo o alrededor de los ojos del Abelisaurus como en otros abelisáuridos encontrados, tal como Carnotaurus, es de suponer que los tuvo, y posiblemente estuvieran hechos de queratina y que por ello no se fosilizó.

facts.statement: The formation containing Abelisaurus remains has been dated to the early Campanian, late Cretaceous, between 83 and 80 million years ago.
facts.quote: Esta ha sido datada en el Campaniano temprano, a finales del Cretácico entre hace 83 a 80 millones de años.

facts.statement: Bonaparte and Novas placed Abelisaurus in its own new family, Abelisauridae, in 1985 within Carnosauria.
facts.quote: Bonaparte y Novas colocaron a Abelisaurus en su propia nueva familia, Abelisauridae, en 1985 dentro de Carnosauria.

facts.statement: Many other abelisaurids have very complete specimens like Aucasaurus, Carnotaurus, and Majungasaurus; thanks to these, it was demonstrated that abelisaurids do not belong to Carnosauria in a modern sense, but instead belong to Neoceratosauria.
facts.quote: Muchos otros abelisáuridos poseen especímenes muy completos como Aucasaurus, Carnotaurus y Majungasaurus; gracias a estos se pudo desmostar que los abelisáuridos no pertenecen a Carnosauria en un sentido moderno, en su lugar pertenecen a Neoceratosauria.

facts.statement: Some scientists consider Abelisaurus a basal abelisaurid outside the subfamily of carnotaurines, while other scientists disagree with this stance.
facts.quote: Algunos científicos consideran a Abelisaurus como un abelisáurido basal, por fuera de la subfamilia de los carnotaurinos, y otros científicos se alejan de esta postura.

facts.statement: In 2015, Filippi et al. created a new clade, Furileusauria, including advanced Brachyrostra, placing Abelisaurus with Aucasaurus in the subfamily Abelisaurinae, thereby nesting Abelisaurus deeply within Abelisauridae as an advanced family member.
facts.quote: En 2015 Filippi et al. en la descripción de Viavenator crearon un nuevo clado, Furileusauria que incluye a los Brachyrostra más avanzados y colocando a Abelisaurus con Aucasaurus en la subfamilia Abelisaurinae, por lo que anidan profundamente a Abelisaurus dentro de Abelisauridae al considerarlo un miembro avanzado de la familia.

facts.statement: In 2022, Agnolín et al. placed Abelisaurus within Carnotaurinae in the clade Brachyrostra, forming a clade together with Aucasaurus.
facts.quote: Agnolín et al. en su descripción de Guemesia de 2022 coloco a Abelisaurus dentro de Carnotaurinae en el clado Brachyrostra, formando un clado junto a Aucasaurus.

facts.statement: It is presumed that, like tyrannosaurs, abelisaurids were the apex predators of their ecosystem.
facts.quote: Se supone que, al igual que los estos, los Abelisaurios eran los depredadores apicales de su ecosistema.

facts.statement: In 2010, Paul proposed that Abelisaurus hunted titanosaurid sauropods.
facts.quote: En 2010, Paul propuso que Abelisaurus cazaba saurópodos titanosauridos.

facts.statement: The Anacleto Formation consists mainly of violet and dark red clay and mud of fluvial origin.
facts.quote: La Formación Anacleto consiste principalmente en arcillas y lodos, de color violeta y rojo oscuro, de origen fluvial.

facts.statement: The genus Abelisaurus was named by Bonaparte in 1984.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Abelisaurus (genus), Bonaparte 1984

facts.statement: Abelisaurus belongs to the subfamily Abelisaurinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Abelisaurinae

facts.statement: Abelisaurus is classified within the family Abelisauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Abelisauridae

facts.statement: Abelisaurus lived during the Maastrichtian stage, between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Only one fossil occurrence of Abelisaurus has been recorded in the Paleobiology Database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 1

rejected.quote: This single known fossil of Abelisaurus consists of a skull, lacking the lower jaws, that is incomplete, especially on the right side.
